recommendation: Keep this no-change audit commit. The current core source already conveys the approved FHIR-47603 rule after later same-family refinements; further changes should only occur through a new work-group decision about responsibility-taking references.
issue_request: FHIR-47603 was Applied/Persuasive with Modification for R6 and asked FHIR-I to clarify whether Group can represent Practitioners, CareTeams, or Organizations taking collective action. The approved resolution replaced the old Organization-exclusion definition with language saying Groups are not typically expected to act collectively or be formally recognized, while family and household Groups are limited exceptions and practitioner/organization collectives should use Organization or CareTeam when collective action is needed.
initial_application: The Jira-tagged source commit 69336fdb743f01d3bb77205b33e95f302d4d40d6 updated source/group/structuredefinition-Group.xml with the approved definition, note, and examples. That applied the seed issue directly to the authoritative Group StructureDefinition surfaces.
additional_context: Later Applied issue FHIR-50525 refined the same wording by moving the detailed family/household examples into the Group Notes section and linking the StructureDefinition description and root definition to group.html#group-usage. FHIR-49851 then aligned Group and Organization boundary text. Those later reconciliations are already represented on the combined branch, and they refine rather than reverse FHIR-47603. source/fhir.ini lists group=Group as an active resource, so the checked StructureDefinition and Group notes are current-build source.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current source/group/structuredefinition-Group.xml contains the clarified non-typical-collective-action definition and note requested by FHIR-47603, and source/group/group-notes.xml contains the approved examples plus the stronger rule that non-family/non-household Groups SHALL NOT be targets of responsibility-taking references. Re-adding the examples to the root definition would duplicate later FHIR-50525 structure and make the machine-readable definition less maintainable.
